newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn tumbles on fund selling, wheat break.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn tumbles on fund selling, wheat break.

text.p: CBOT corn futures tumbled in fast dealings on fund selling and a sharp break in wheat, traders said.
"Wheat broke. Selling spilled right out of the wheat into corn," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Pit sources said Griffin Trading and Refco Inc each sold at least one million bushels on the break.
Traders said the additional corn sales took Griffin's daily total up to seven million bushels of July corn sold.
Wheat futures rallied near midday on news the European Union slapped a 15-ecu tax on soft wheat exports.

But wheat collapsed amid talk of yet another U.S. hard red winter wheat damage estimate. Floor sources said the latest estimate put damage from a recent freeze at 100 million to 117 million bushels, well below earlier predictions for up to 290 million bushels lost.
At 1232 CDT, corn was down 5-1/2 to 2-3/4 cents per bushel with May off four at $2.94-1/2.
Wheat was down 5-1/4 to two cents per bushel with July off 5-1/4 at $4.30-1/2.
